blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of reaction
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy of a reaction, delta Hr, is the enthalpy change when stoichiometric amounts of reactants in their standard states react together completely to form products under standard conditions.
For example, hydrogen and oxygen forming one mole of water: H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) gives H2O(l), delta Hr = -286 kJ per mol.
